claims.text: NØNOS treats every program as untrusted until it is proved.
to_establish: What exactly is proved: which statement, by whom, checked against which root?
Does the proof say anything about what the program does, or only that it is the enrolled program?

claims.text: A program that cannot prove what it is does not run.
to_establish: Is there any path that starts a program without the proof check: boot-time capsules, the Linux personality, development profiles?

claims.text: Each capsule meets eleven checks at spawn, in order, and is refused at the first one it fails.
to_establish: List the eleven checks with file and line.
Confirm the order and that no check can be skipped by any profile or feature.

claims.text: Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65, both required, over the signed region.
to_establish: Show that both are required on every path, including the older trailer format.
Which bytes are the signed region, and what is outside it?

claims.text: A capsule can only ever lose authority at this step, never gain it.
to_establish: Show the intersection of request, manifest and boot profile in code.
Can any later step add authority?

claims.text: The proof is a transparent, hash-based STARK over the Goldilocks field with a FRI low-degree test: no trusted setup, no powers-of-tau ceremony, no toxic waste that someone has to be trusted to have destroyed.
to_establish: Verifier parameters and the security level they give.
Is the claim of no trusted setup true of the whole chain, including the enrolled roots?

claims.text: The boot checks the kernel's STARK proof before it starts anything.
to_establish: What is the order of checks in the loader, and what runs before the proof is checked?

claims.text: The bootloader verifies the kernel with two independent signatures, one of them post-quantum, then checks the kernel's own proof against a root baked into the bootloader.
to_establish: Where is the root baked in, and what protects it from replacement?

claims.text: The client checks the host's two signatures, its TPM quote and its boot chain before any credential is sent.
to_establish: What does the client check when the host has no TPM or reports a self-reported boot?

claims.text: Anything not on the list is refused, and the log says why.
to_establish: Is every capability check in the kernel, or can a service grant more than its manifest lists?

claims.text: Five properties hold over every state the kernel can reach, tied to the Rust that ships.
to_establish: Name the five properties and the theorems.
What does reachable mean in the model, and what is excluded from it?

claims.text: NØNOS proves the code.
to_establish: Which code, and which properties? State the gap between the extracted functions and the whole kernel.

claims.text: 1,174 functions are extracted and proved this way.
to_establish: Reproduce the count from the evidence file at a pinned commit.

claims.text: Of the 1,174, 533 carry a property about what the function does; 641 carry only the theorem that a generated wrapper is the method it forwards to; none are left unproven.
to_establish: Reproduce both counts.
Spot-check that the 533 properties are not trivially true.

claims.text: the specification corpus holds 1,604 theorems and lemmas in 201 Lean files with no sorry anywhere, 115 Kani harnesses over the crypto and parser paths
to_establish: Reproduce each count.
Check every Kani bound is backed by an unwinding assertion.

claims.text: Memory is wiped when you power off, and nothing is written to a disk unless you install.
to_establish: What is wiped, by what mechanism, and when: orderly shutdown only, or also a crash or a power cut?
Test that a live session writes no block to any attached disk.

claims.text: It runs from memory, checks every program before it starts, and forgets everything at power-off.
to_establish: Does anything survive: firmware variables, the TPM, NVRAM, a USB stick the user attaches?

claims.text: no telemetry because there is no switch for it.
to_establish: Measure all egress of an idle machine over a day, by destination and capsule.
Compare the result with the egress list in the privacy documentation.

claims.text: a random MAC address at each start
to_establish: Is the randomised address used for every frame, including before the setup screen and during DHCP?

claims.text: NØNOS links no third-party anonymity client.
to_establish: Confirm from the dependency graph and the image contents.

claims.text: so what each learns ends with the boot.
to_establish: What does each transport store, and where? Test that no file is written.

claims.text: NØNOS runs unmodified x86_64 Linux programs as capsules.
to_establish: Where does the Linux personality sit in the trust chain, and what can a guest reach?

claims.text: so the conversation never leaves the machine to be fast enough.
to_establish: Test that inference makes no network request, and that the model capsule holds no network capability.

claims.text: The kernel starts every CPU the firmware brings up, up to 256, and schedules processes across all of them from one run queue.
to_establish: What was the largest CPU count actually tested?
Is a single run queue a scaling limit or an isolation risk?

claims.text: five families are proven on real hardware.
to_establish: Which hardware, which firmware versions, and where is the evidence?
What does proven mean here: a boot, or a defined test suite?

claims.text: so a rebuild on any machine now measures to the enrolled trust
to_establish: Rebuild on two machines and compare. List what differs.
